entries.label: Version 1
entries.prompt:
Create a high-fidelity, browser-viewable, clickable UI prototype for resolving GitHub issue "Prototype the Galaxy Z Fold6 Android experience". This is throwaway design work only, not production app code.

Build an interactive FermentStation household fermentation tracker concept for a Galaxy Z Fold6. Preserve the established visual direction: warm editorial household-craft styling; tactile paper/clay character; calm, practical information hierarchy; shared batch-status colors; Android-native interactions and accessibility. Use the existing recovered prototype only as visual reference if available; do not overwrite or alter it.

The single artifact must let a reviewer compare three structurally different adaptive layout variants, switchable in a clearly labeled prototype-only fixed bottom switcher and with left/right keyboard navigation. The variation must be in hierarchy and layout, not merely color:
A. Cover display: compact Today-first list; inner display: navigation rail plus detail pane.
B. Cover display: task-oriented home; inner display: dashboard canvas with persistent batch queue.
C. Cover display: timeline-focused navigation; inner display: multi-column workbench.

For every variant, make the cover screen approximately 23:9 narrow portrait and the inner display approximately 6:5 wide. Provide an obvious posture toggle that keeps the same active primary destination and retains any visible unsaved draft text when switching cover/inner. Demonstrate this by allowing the user to start a timeline entry or batch note, type text, navigate between primary destinations, and fold/unfold without losing it.

Cover all primary navigation: Today, Batches, Calendar, Profiles, and Settings. Include believable sample content for active, ready, and to-fridge batches. Cover Android interaction states: selected nav state, FAB or primary action, bottom sheet/dialog editing, focus/typing state, empty or no-results state, and an accessible status presentation not dependent only on color. Use touch-friendly targets and label controls.

Place a short in-prototype note identifying this as a review-only Fold6 concept and how to switch variants/posture. Make it self-contained HTML/CSS/JS, runnable directly in the preview. Aim to create a concrete concept the user can critique, not an implementation plan.
